phase.label: Phase 1
phase.subtitle: Compliance concerns
phase.summary: Refined Phase 1 evidential modelling retained from the original prototype, covering operational case concerns, internal communications, training context, and the initial move into grievance handling.

items.title: Silence treated as consent to contract
items.summary: Operational case marker used to show the early compliance concern sequence in macro and phase views.
items.body: After a customer stated they had not consented to a contract, the record of a contract email being sent was treated as sufficient verification. The Phase 1 implementation retains this as a key compliance concern example.
items.source_wording: Customer non-consent concern linked to contract email record treatment.
items.related_report_section: 1. MS Teams Evidence / 2. Systemic & Cultural Evidence
items.investigator_note: One of the earliest chronology anchors for the Phase 1 band, retained so the macro view shows the dossier story beginning with compliance concerns.

items.title: Teams message raising vague guidance concern
items.summary: Communication marker showing that the chronology is not only case handling but also contemporaneous internal escalation.
items.body: The message records concern that only vague guidance had been received, placing the handler in a difficult position with customers.
items.quote: I've only received very vague guidance which puts me in a difficult position with customers.
items.investigator_note: Retained to show the chronology as an evidential bridge between operational handling and management awareness.

items.title: Complaint closed despite customer instruction
items.summary: Complaint handling marker showing the cumulative pattern inside Phase 1.
items.body: The complaint was closed even though the customer indicated it should remain open until the issue was resolved. This remains a core dossier example for complaint handling concerns.
items.source_wording: Complaint remained unresolved but closure occurred.
items.related_report_section: 1. MS Teams Evidence / 2. Systemic & Cultural Evidence
items.investigator_note: Supports the shift from isolated cases into a broader pattern argument.

items.title: Translator refused and ADR route blocked
items.summary: High-priority operational marker preserved so the macro view shows escalation in the seriousness of concerns.
items.body: A vulnerable customer linked the debt issue to a language barrier. The complaint was to be closed without mention of ADR despite the unresolved issue.
items.source_wording: Translator / language support concern linked to debt and complaint handling.
items.related_report_section: 1. MS Teams Evidence / 2. Systemic & Cultural Evidence
items.investigator_note: Used as a major Phase 1 anchor because it links operational evidence to vulnerability and ADR concerns.

items.title: Complaints training session
items.summary: The training event is kept as a documentary hinge between case examples and the report's dedicated training analysis section.
items.body: WebEx complaints training promoted rapid complaint closure and adviser-led resolution. The detailed analysis remains a report-section destination rather than a timeline replacement.
items.source_wording: Back to Basics complaints training session placeholder summary.
items.investigator_note: Links the timeline into the dedicated training analysis route.

items.title: Teams message referencing Ofcom responsibilities
items.summary: Placed alongside the training marker to show documentary overlap between training context and contemporaneous communication.
items.body: The DM records concern about closing the complaint while emphasising the responsibility to be aware of Ofcom regulations.
items.quote: Part of my responsibility as an agent is to be aware of Ofcom's regulations.
items.related_report_section: 1. MS Teams Evidence / 3. Complaints Training Session
items.related_dossier_page: Report section 3.2 training and practice comparison
items.investigator_note: Useful at evidence zoom because it ties the timeline back into the report analysis without duplicating the full section content.

items.title: Initial email to HR
items.summary: Separated from the GH-01 transmission marker to preserve chronology certainty and avoid conflating a floating layout note with a confirmed sent item.
items.body: Outlines difficulties and requests a change of team or department. This remains modelled as approximate from layout rather than a hard-anchored dated transmission.
items.source_wording: Initial email to HR outlining difficulties and requested move.
items.investigator_note: Important fidelity correction retained from the Phase 1 prototype.

items.title: GH-01 transmission marker
items.summary: The confirmed sent marker begins the grievance correspondence line and bridges Phase 1 into Phase 2.
items.body: Confirmed transmission marker retained separately from the floating HR email note, allowing later grievance handling phases to build on a clean chronology.
items.investigator_note: Critical for continuity because it starts the grievance correspondence route.

items.title: Vulnerable customer escalation
items.summary: The final major Phase 1 marker shows the chronology escalating immediately before the grievance-focused phases.
items.body: An elderly customer reported a more expensive package after an in-store visit. The complaint was closed without permission and without resolution, preventing ADR access.
items.source_wording: 85-year-old widow complaint closure and vulnerability concern.
items.related_report_section: 1. MS Teams Evidence / 2. Systemic & Cultural Evidence
items.investigator_note: Used in macro view to show the dossier story as cumulative and escalating before Phase 2 begins.
